questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How dyslexia can bring useful skills at work
How to teach young children to spell well
Why reading on trains is good for your brain
The life and work of Albert Einstein
questions.why: They hear how dyslexics have other skills which let them excel in the workplace.

questions.q: How are Phil's and Pippa's reading habits different?
options: Phil reads every day; Pippa rarely reads at all
They both read only at weekends, in bed
Neither of them enjoys reading very much
Pippa reads on the train; Phil sometimes stops
questions.why: Phil sometimes goes a while without reading; Pippa loves to read on the train to work.

questions.q: Roughly how many people in the UK are thought to be dyslexic?
options: One in a hundred
One in three
About one in ten
Half of all people
questions.why: Phil says it's thought around one in ten people in the UK are dyslexic.

questions.q: Why do many dyslexic children struggle at school?
options: Their teachers don't like them
School focuses mainly on reading and writing
They are not good at problem solving
They miss a lot of lessons
questions.why: Phil says many dyslexic children struggle at school, 'where the focus is on reading and writing'.

questions.q: What is the message of the video by celebrities like Orlando Bloom and Keira Knightley?
options: Dyslexic people should become actors
Dyslexia can be cured with the right help
Dyslexia makes normal life impossible
Dyslexia is a different way of thinking
questions.why: They say dyslexia is 'your superpower', the way you think, and different views are vital.

questions.q: What did the report co-written by Kate Griggs show?
options: Supporting dyslexic workers could add billions
Most dyslexic people work as spies or soldiers
Dyslexic workers earn much less than others
Very few companies employ dyslexic people
questions.why: Pippa says the report showed empowering dyslexic workers could boost the global economy by billions.

questions.q: Why does Kate Griggs talk about spies?
options: Because she used to work as one herself
To show dyslexic skills help in some jobs
To warn people about terror threats
Because spies don't need to read or write
questions.why: Spies must read people, spot patterns and solve problems quickly, so 'dyslexics are brilliant spies'.

questions.q: What does Dr Maggie Aderin-Pocock believe helps teams succeed?
options: Choosing only the best and fastest readers
Working alone on the most difficult problems
Valuing everyone's different skills
Having a very strict leader who decides
questions.why: She says it's about recognising people's skills and differences, and valuing all the skills.
